title: G-7 Agrees to Release 100 Million Barrels of Reserve Diesel
gist: The G-7 agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude reserves over four months — about one day of global oil demand, front-loaded with diesel within 20 days — after Trump threatened to ban U.S. diesel exports unless France and Germany drew down their own stocks. With U.S. diesel above $6 a gallon and Trump's cost-of-living approval at 17% before the midterms, it is unclear the release will suffice; the brief also covers French student unrest over a debt-squeezed budget and Congo's 4,000-death Ebola outbreak.

insights.claim: G-7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from reserves over four months — roughly one day of global oil demand — including a 'frontloaded substantial diesel release' within 20 days, monitored by the IEA.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Near-term downward pressure on diesel cracks, but the volume is small relative to the supply disruption.

insights.claim: French student protests demanding education investment have closed around 400 high schools, led to about 3,000 arrests, and been worsened by a controversial 2027 budget in which debt-servicing costs are expected to overtake education as France's largest budget item.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Debt service crowding out spending fuels social unrest and political risk ahead of France's next general election — relevant for OAT spreads.
insights.quote: Although education is typically France’s largest budget item, debt-servicing costs are expected to take the No. 1 spot next year.

insights.claim: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 4,000 with about 8,300 confirmed cases since May 15, the second-largest outbreak after 2014-2016, driven by the Bundibugyo strain for which there is no known vaccine or treatment.
insights.speaker: Alexandra Sharp
insights.so_what: Uncontained outbreak poses regional health and mining-region disruption risk in eastern Congo.
